public_rationale: The available tests support serious reliability limitations. They do not settle the whole statement. OpenAI also reported substantial success on browser benchmarks, including the more complex WebArena. Aggregate scores do not identify whether successful tasks were simple, and the statement gives no standard for disqualification. The Anthropic launch evidence predates the target window.
limitations: The strongest broad results are vendor-reported.
The independent failure demonstrations cover only five tasks.
Benchmark performance is not interchangeable with unattended production reliability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's and Anthropic's computer-use agents are unreliable to the point of being disqualifying and only succeed at simple tasks.

statement.excerpt: In OpenAI and Anthropic’s case, “agents” refer to a model that controls your computer and performs tasks based on a prompt. This is closer to “the truth,” other than the fact it’s so unreliable as to be disqualifying, and the tasks it succeeds at (like searching on Tripadvisor) are remarkably simple.

from_speaker: a model that controls your computer and performs tasks based on a prompt
so unreliable as to be disqualifying
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that the then-current computer-use agents cannot be depended on for unattended general computer work, with successful demonstrations concentrated in ordinary simple tasks.
Assess January 1 through February 24, 2025: the latest complete month and the current partial month before the post.
Do not interpret the statement as a forecast about later agent versions.
'Disqualifying' is read in the surrounding context of autonomous task execution, not as claiming the products have no possible supervised use.
Whether 'the tasks it succeeds at' means exclusively simple tasks or predominantly simple demonstrations is unresolved.
criteria.support_condition: Representative tests show frequent failures in unattended ordinary computer work, while task-level results show successful performance concentrated in simple tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative tests establish dependable unattended performance and substantial successful completion of complex computer workflows by the then-current products.

evidence.explanation: The OSWorld result supports substantial unreliability in general computer tasks. The same disclosure reports 58.1% on the more complex WebArena and 87% on the simpler WebVoyager, which cautions against treating all successful performance as trivial.

evidence.publisher: Zengyi Qin, published on Hugging Face
evidence.explanation: The author's dated tests show failures involving image editing, locating problems and operating online tools. Five demonstrations support the existence of serious failures but cannot estimate representative reliability or characterize all successes.

evidence.excerpt: At this stage, it is still experimental—at times cumbersome and error-prone.
evidence.locator: Opening description of the computer-use public beta
evidence.explanation: Anthropic itself acknowledged early computer-use limitations. This establishes the launch context, but the earlier date prevents treating it as a fresh measurement during January–February 2025.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Task-level evaluations of both contemporary products, recording complexity and human intervention, interpreted against an explicit practical standard for dependable autonomous use.
